name: Spanram
silhouette: A tall long-legged ram with two high buttress horns joining above its brow, a narrow waist and two strong negative-space arches.
motion: High deliberate diagonal hoof steps; horns sway opposite hips.

name: Tuftpika
silhouette: A tiny pika with long swept-back grass whiskers, round ears, a square leafy tail tuft and two high-set dark eyes.
motion: Compact four-paw gallop, pause, whisker flick.

name: Rootmuffle
silhouette: A low long-bodied pika with a broad root beard and two separated leafy shoulder mounds; its ears and living muzzle remain exposed.
motion: Low belly-clear scamper; beard trails, then gathers beneath chin.

name: Sporevault
silhouette: An upright long-hindleg pika with a closed pinecone tail carried above its head and a tiny chest between large open arm spaces.
motion: Crouch, tall hop, two-foot settle; tail opens only during casting.

name: Chalklung
silhouette: A living porous sponge with three soft lobed feet, one angled chimney and a friendly face on its lower flexible skirt.
motion: Three-foot rocking walk; chimney compresses and rebounds as it breathes.

name: Bellcup
silhouette: A tall sponge with an inverted bell mouth, a long curved neck, broad two-lobed base and a face looking out beneath the rim.
motion: Leans forward on the base, straightens neck, then draws the base underneath.

name: Runnelribbon
silhouette: A flat ribbon sponge with two raised breathing sails, four stub feet and a living face at one blunt leading corner.
motion: Sideways inchworm fold, unfold and soft skirt sweep.

name: Orelet
silhouette: A round mole with a pale snout, narrow metallic digging nails and one smooth ore nodule at the tip of its very short tail.
motion: Alternating outward forepaw scoops with its feet visibly above the ground.

name: Augermole
silhouette: A long wedge-bodied mole whose broad serrated forepaws frame a low face; its body tapers into a small straight tail.
motion: Wide shoulder crawl with nails swept behind during recovery.

name: Pendulumole
silhouette: An upright mole with long forearms, broad planted hindfeet and an elongated heavy tail curved into a counterweight loop.
motion: Two hindfoot steps then tail counter-swing; face aims independently of arms.

name: Ashkite
silhouette: A planthopper with a broad kite-shaped shell, very short antennae, tucked legs and a visible round face below a shallow hood.
motion: Tiny spring hop, side slip and four-foot landing.

name: Plumehopper
silhouette: A tall long-legged hopper with a narrow upright plume, a pear-shaped abdomen and an open diamond between its rear legs.
motion: High tucked-leg spring, upright hover beat and heel-first landing.

name: Huskdrifter
silhouette: A broad leaf-shaped hopper held horizontally beneath translucent folded shell sails, with a small face extending beyond their front edge.
motion: Low skirt-like glide with visible occasional leg taps; not a permanent flight permission.

name: Inkbud
silhouette: A teardrop cuttlefish with a blunt living face, six short arm tips and two long bracket feelers; dark mantle separated from pale fins.
motion: Mantle pulses forward, fins ripple left-to-right, feelers catch up.

name: Scriptcuttle
silhouette: A long rectangular cuttlefish mantle between two scalloped fin rails; four long arms curl into open brackets beneath its large eyes.
motion: Long steady fin-wave glide, then separate left and right bracket-arm folds.

name: Fanfolio
silhouette: A broad cuttlefish with joined webbed arms spread into two offset fans; the face sits in a deep central V, with a short mantle behind.
motion: Alternating broad fan strokes, a sideways bank, and a deliberate web fold.

name: Bobclam
silhouette: A living rounded clam with two unequal chalk valves, a visible smiling hinge face and one thick scalloped foot.
motion: Foot reaches, shell tips forward, valves clap gently after the pull.

name: Keelcasket
silhouette: A long low clam with an open split-keel lower valve, broad muscular foot and an eye-bearing upper lip projecting forward.
motion: Low foot ripples while the keel rocks in opposite phase; eyelids track the path.

name: Crownfloat
silhouette: A tall clam with two thin high valves held in an open crown above its face; a short inflated foot forms a visible round ballast below.
motion: Foot inflates for a short buoyant rise then settles; valves open asymmetrically.

name: Frondfoal
silhouette: An upright seahorse with a leaf-frilled short snout, two small fins and a single hook tail with a bare visible tip.
motion: Two fin flutters, forward nod and uncoiling tail step without a static hover.

name: Trellisseer
silhouette: A tall seahorse whose paired branching back fronds frame an open ladder behind its small living face; long nearly straight tail.
motion: Long upright fin strokes; the tail straightens and the open frond ladder flexes.

name: Bowercoil
silhouette: A compact seahorse curled sideways around one broad living kelp loop, head outside the loop and fins above its low center.
motion: Tail hooks, releases and rolls one quarter-turn while the face remains upright.

name: Rimlet
silhouette: A low horseshoe-crab animal with a smooth U-shaped metal rim, two bright front eyes, six tiny feet and a slender jointed tail.
motion: Six feet scuttle in offset pairs, tail steers late and the rim dips.

name: Gateshield
silhouette: A narrow horseshoe body whose two upright rim halves form an open portal around its face; splayed rear feet and a fork-ended tail.
motion: Diagonal braced steps, opening rim halves and a two-beat gate-close gesture.
